head: d72d1af1eb7b9a3cd60b0acb5364689e16735ea5
summary: The focused Python and Unity protocol suites pass, but the current live collector path is not release-safe. Request 38 and request 70 use one ScienceBirdsBridge even though request 70 is served by a separate one-request Unity socket; multi-frame persistence reuses that closed connection; temporary-shot symlinks can survive recovery and redirect writes; and completed shots are reused without comparing their provenance to the requested hashes.

evidence: scripts/collect_rollouts.py:1591-1605 sends request 38 through the collector bridge.
scripts/collect_rollouts.py:1633 calls capture_physics_rollout with that same bridge.
src/webui/bridge.py:201-214 sends request 70 through the bridge socket.
tasks/task_template_designer/Assets/Scripts/AIBirdsConnection.cs:1634-1654 attaches a separate direct physics listener, default port 2004, while gameplay uses its websocket port.
scripts/collect_rollouts.py:1947-1949 exposes only one host/port for the collector bridge and has no independent physics endpoint.
release_blockers.impact: A production collection cannot reliably issue gameplay requests and direct physics captures over their required transports.

evidence: scripts/physics_rollout_persistence.py:154-158 calls get_physics_capture_v1 repeatedly on one bridge for every frame.
tasks/task_template_designer/Assets/Scripts/GroundTruth/PhysicsCaptureProtocol.cs:344-376 serves one request and closes the TcpClient in finally.
src/webui/bridge.py:118-124 keeps the socket until an explicit disconnect and does not reconnect before the next request.
release_blockers.impact: Any capture requiring more than one frame fails after the first direct request-70 response.

evidence: scripts/collect_rollouts.py:940-947 deliberately leaves shot_*.tmp symlinks in place.
scripts/collect_rollouts.py:1545-1547 accepts an existing temporary path with mkdir(exist_ok=True).
scripts/physics_rollout_persistence.py:139-144 creates frames and sidecar paths before any temporary-root symlink confinement check.
release_blockers.impact: A pre-existing shot_NNN.tmp symlink can redirect collector writes outside the output root.

evidence: scripts/collect_rollouts.py:1522-1541 reuses any internally valid completed shot and continues without comparing metadata provenance to physics_player_sha256, physics_protocol_sha256, or physics_archive_sha256.
The manifest is then populated with the current requested hashes at scripts/collect_rollouts.py:1734-1737, allowing reused shot metadata and manifest provenance to disagree.
release_blockers.impact: A valid artifact from an older player/protocol/archive can be silently accepted under new provenance.

coverage: oversized sidecar rejection before JSONL parsing

manual_pacing.result: passed with injected clock and sleeper

unity_protocol.note: Both XML files completed successfully. The Unity editor hung after results were written because of the known post-test CEF shutdown/core-dump behavior.

request 38 before request 70 and exact request bytes
criterion_results.status: passed in mocks, failed as a live transport design

criterion_results.criterion: Unity global pending/in-flight cap and timeout release

worktree_integrity.details: The worktree was already heavily dirty. During this verification, scripts/rollout_artifacts.py and tests/test_collect_rollouts.py changed from their captured baseline hashes. The focused Python matrix was rerun twice after those changes; scoped final hashes were recaptured.

required_repairs: Give gameplay and physics capture separate explicitly configured connections, and route requests 38/62 to gameplay while routing request 70 to the direct physics socket.
Reconnect for every direct request-70 call or change the Unity direct server to support multiple request-response cycles per connection, with a live multi-frame test.
Reject or quarantine any shot_*.tmp symlink before mkdir or writes; use descriptor-based no-follow creation for the temporary root and children.
Compare completed-shot metadata provenance to the currently requested player, protocol, and archive hashes before reuse; quarantine mismatches.
